title: Sources
text:

apollo15-pds-lsrp
acquired
Apollo 15 Lunar Module Soil Mechanics Data Bundle
A15L-L-LSRP-2/3-SOIL-MECHANICS-V1.0; urn:nasa:pds:a15lsrp_soil_mechanics
2012 archive citation; measurements 1971
document/a15_lsrp_data_report.pdf: 32 pages; document/a15_psr_ch7_sm.pdf: 29 pages
Data sets archived in the PDS are in the public domain. (Archive explicitly states public domain)
Drum readings; calibrated load; stress; penetration depth for cone and plate operations; data form: raw; tests: Six runs; four cone and two plate runs; data pages: Data directory; dataset_description.txt; instrument document a15l_lsrp.txt; six station-8 runs
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire-with-caveat; setup recoverability medium; text layer: Plain ASCII table sampled successfully; includes transcribed instrument readings and reduced values. Caveat: hand transcription from microfilm; uncertain in situ density and operator-controlled rate; reference-pad movement affects depth. Archive describes corrections. Direct URL is one file; siblings in the data directory supply the other runs. Distinguish experiment year from archive publication. Download: https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lunar/urn-nasa-pds-a15lsrp_soil_mechanics/data/a15_smss_71_m016935_011.tab Lead found by both.

wes-m71-10-rpt1
acquired
Performance of Boeing LRV wheels in a lunar soil simulant. Report 1: Effect of wheel design and soil
M-71-10 Report 1; NASA-CR-127695; supersedes M-70-15
1971
86
Distribution Limits: Public; Copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted. (NTRS explicitly identifies government work and permits public use)
Wheel pull; torque; slip; sinkage; soil density; moisture; cone resistance; triaxial and plate-shear measurements; data form: tables; tests: Six wheel designs; four soil conditions; dozens of wheel runs; six vacuum-triaxial and eight plate-shear tests described; data pages: Part II printed 3-9/PDF 11-17; Part III printed 10-16/PDF 18-24; Tables 1-5; Table 3 sample PDF 66
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire; setup recoverability high; text layer: Prose OCR usable; Table 3 numerical OCR badly degraded. Detailed wheel geometry, crushed-basalt preparation, soil state and test procedures are documented. Numeric extraction must use original images. Legacy PDF URL failed; current NTRS download worked. Soil characterization and wheel tests must remain separate series. Download: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720021195/downloads/19720021195.pdf Lead found by claude.

M-71-10 Report 2; NASA-CR-129612; correct NTRS 19730004536
1971
97
Distribution Limits: Public; Copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted. (NTRS explicitly identifies government work and permits public use)
Pull; torque; slip; sinkage; wheel speed and acceleration; load; cone gradient; density; moisture; data form: tables; tests: Two wheel designs and two phases; dozens of runs; seven ramped-slip and eight multi-programmed-slip runs explicitly described in Phase I; data pages: Part II printed 3-18/PDF 16-31; Part III printed 19-51/PDF 32-64; Tables 1-8 after text; Table 1 PDF 68 in 97-page copy
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire; setup recoverability high; text layer: OCR usable for prose and some tables; check numerical columns against images. Corrected identity: supplied 19720007590 is Mullis’s dust-profile report. Setup recovery depends partly on Report 1. Some soil strengths are inherited from earlier work. Keep page maps separate for the 97-page and 89-page files. Download: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19730004536/downloads/19730004536.pdf Lead found by claude.


apollo-s200-final-1974
located
Apollo soil mechanics experiment S-200
NASA-CR-134306; SSL Series 15 Issue 7
1974
135 PDF pages
Distribution Limits: Public; Copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted. (NTRS explicitly identifies government work and permits public use)
Grain-size distributions; specific gravity; minimum and maximum density; core density; penetration and compression results; derived porosity and strength; data form: tables; tests: Multiple missions and laboratory samples; Table 3-9 summarizes 776 footprint observations, not 776 controlled tests; data pages: Chapter 3; Table 3-3 printed 31/PDF 40; Table 3-5 printed 38/PDF 47; Table 3-9 printed 56/PDF 65
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire-with-caveat; setup recoverability medium; text layer: OCR readable with substantial symbol and digit errors; sampled tables require image verification. Caveat: synthesis mixes direct measurements, correlations and inferred properties. Original tests may recur in mission reports and PDS. Setup varies by source; build explicit same-test and derived-from relations before calibration. Download: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19740019219/downloads/19740019219.pdf Lead found by claude.


arslan-2007-lasp105525
located
JSC-1a Geotechnical Properties Experiments: Tons 1, 2, 3
LASP 105525 Rev. A
2007
74 PDF pages
no statement found; inspected cover and front matter and searched extracted text for copyright and permission (NASA hosting alone does not establish the report’s license)
Sieve fractions; dry density; triaxial stress and strain; peak strength; tensile response; data form: tables; tests: Nine sieve tests; three triaxial density levels by three confinement levels with replicates; Tables 5-6 alone list 31 runs; data pages: Section 2 printed 14-24/PDF 16-26; Tables 1-3 printed 15/PDF 17; Tables 5-7 printed 19-21/PDF 21-23; Appendices A-C
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire-with-caveat; setup recoverability high; text layer: Text layer usable; tables and prose sampled. Caveat: rights unclear. Strong setup description: specimen geometry, layered preparation, confinement and loading rate. Some reported specimens were reused after earlier loading, so material history must be preserved. Appendices contain individual test records and figure locators. Download: https://ares.jsc.nasa.gov/projects/simulants/attachments/JSC-1A_LASP_Geotech_Properties_Tons1-3.pdf Lead found by both.

dotson-2024-shear
located
Cohesion and Shear Strength of Compacted Lunar and Martian Regolith Simulants
arXiv:2403.11029; 10.48550/arXiv.2403.11029
2024
23 PDF pages; submission approximately 2287 KB
CC0 1.0 Universal (arXiv license link resolves to CC0; do not substitute CC BY)
Particle-size and shape measures; direct-shear peak stress; density; fitted cohesion and friction; data form: tables; tests: Eleven simulants plus two glass controls and an additional dried condition; multiple densities; at least four normal stresses per density; data pages: Methods Section 2; Results Section 3; Tables 2-3 printed/PDF 8-9; shear-data figure locators thereafter
Screened 2026-10-07 by codex (gpt-6-astra), text and metadata only: verdict acquire-with-caveat; setup recoverability medium; text layer: Usable PDF text layer; sampled methods and tables. Caveat: numerical shear rate was not recovered from inspected methods and ambient moisture was uncontrolled. Geometry and normal-load range are described. Much mechanical output is peak-strength reduction, not a downloadable full stress-displacement history. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.11029 Lead found by codex.

10.57745/NTSZ8G; Version 2
2026

Etalab Open License 2.0, compatible CC-BY 2.0 (Indexed repository explicitly lists Etalab Open License 2.0; not CC BY 4.0)
Catalogue advertises compiled regolith and simulant properties plus particle-size data; file values uninspected; data form: parameters-only; tests: 24 observations listed for simulant table; this is not an independent-test count; data pages: Listed Dataset_All.csv; Dataset_Regolith.csv; Dataset_Samples.csv; Dataset_Samples_PSD.csv; Dataset_Simulants.tab; README.md

Caveat: secondary compilation and inaccessible files. Grade is provisional from catalogue evidence; PSD file may contain measured distributions, so do not conclude parameters-only for the entire bundle. Use as a source crosswalk, not an independent validation set. Lead found by both.

title: b68-ds-fa-40: provenance
text:
Notes from the two readings

Claude: Cross-hatched band 40 to 45 deg, no curve: loose LSM densified under the normal load so no phi vs Dr curve could be drawn (A-79; A-88). Band drawn across Dr 0 to 1.0 although the text limits it to Dr .40 to 1.00. Same band as FC-21 without the markers. Text phi: soil 10 about 42; soil 11 about 38.3 (outside the band; Table 2-3 42). Reprinted under soil 11.
Codex: Estimated 40 to 45 degree scatter band; no mean curve. Text limits interpretation to Dr .40 to 1.00 although band spans plot. A-84 gives 38.3 degrees for soil 11. Geometry and rate missing. AM-68-1 Vol. II, Fig. A-40, printed A-78, PDF 79

title: Open questions
text:
This data set is a first step in a longer journey, not a finished product. The numbers come from scanned reports more than half a century old, read twice by independent agents, reconciled by rule, and sampled by student auditors. That process leaves questions we could not settle, and a few we chose not to spend more time on yet. They are listed here so that a user knows where the soft spots are, and so that anyone who wants to help can pick one up. If you can answer one, open an issue or a pull request in the repository, or write to the maintainers; a better scan, a printed copy of a report, or an hour with a figure on your screen is enough to close several of them.
A reading uncertainty on this site is the uncertainty of our reading of the printed figure, not the uncertainty of the experiment. Nothing below changes that distinction.

title: Open questions
text:
Reading the figures

Trace samples in gaps. A sampled point on a plotted curve should sit on the line’s own ink, not on a symbol or in the white gap between a dash and a symbol. A mechanical check now removes samples that fail this (it was validated blind on 400 samples: 98 percent of what it removes is rightly removed), but it finds only about half of the failures. The misses are at curve ends on the frame or a grid line, and at junctions where a symbol’s outline fuses with the line. About 300 samples it could not decide are kept and marked for review. See qa/adjudication-2026-10-28-inkrule/review.md and tools/check_trace_ink.py.
Symbols merged with grid lines or with each other. For 22 points of the first audit wave, two rounds of blind re-reading could not say where the symbol’s center is (8 undecided, 14 still split within a pixel). They are in the data with widened bounds and the status pending-review. See qa/adjudication-2026-10-27/review.md.
Which point of a triangle the 1968 plotter registered. A plotted triangle has two defensible centers, its centroid and the middle of its bounding box, about one sixth of its height apart. We accept both and carry the difference in the bound (docs/CURVE-READING.md, rule 8). A page of the report or of the plotter’s manual that states the convention would tighten every marker.
Grain-size bands that merge. On the Appendix A grain-size charts the average curve and the two range curves run together over parts of their length, and neither reader could tell them apart there. See insights/1968-vol2-appendix-a-grain-size-curves-against-their-tables.md.
Residual labels on log and reciprocal axes. One item of the axis transform work (D-027) remains: the site labels residuals in printed units rather than in the transformed coordinate. Values and verdicts are unaffected. The other two items are done (2026-11-18): the canonical files now record where the other reading lies on the page, and audit packets draw it there, instead of placing it with a map fitted to the kept reading.

title: Open questions
text:
The printed sources themselves

Seven cells of Table 2-2 (Volume I, printed 2-14). The page is a 200 dpi bilevel scan on which 5, 6 and 8 print alike. The cells carry both readings. A better scan or a printed copy of AM-68-1 Volume I would settle them. See qa/pages-s2-b1/review.md.
Table 2-3 against the Appendix A specifications. The summary table of Volume I and the per-soil specification sheets of Volume II disagree on six friction angles (soils 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 12) and on the gradations of four soils; 26 cells differ in all. Both Volcalite reprints are misprinted and the first printing is right. We record both values and do not know which the authors used downstream. See qa/specifications/table23-vs-appendix-a.md.
The Table 2-3 modulus. It appears to be IITRI’s small-strain wave modulus, interpolated in relative density from two tested densities. This is an inference from the Appendix B plots, not a statement in the report.
Computer plots against their printed fits. On the Appendix C computer plots (Figs. C-8 to C-15) the drawn least-squares lines depart from the fit parameters printed on the same plot by up to 96 psf, while the printed parameters reproduce from the data sheets. We do not know why the plotter drew the lines where it did. See insights/1968-vol2-appendix-c-computer-plots-against-printed-fits.md.
Relations between records that could not be resolved. Five items of the Volume II figure index carry the relation unresolved (the Soil No. 10 specification table, printed A-71, PDF 72, and Figs. C-12 to C-15): each appears to repeat material printed elsewhere, but the evidence does not say whether it is the same item or a derived one (for example Fig. C-12 against data sheet C-4B). They are counted once, on the side of caution. (Corrected 2026-11-05: this item said 31 rows of the experiment index; that index has no unresolved relation, only same-as and derived-from.)
Setup fields. Many records do not yet carry a complete setup (apparatus, rate, sample preparation) because the report prints it once for a family and the index has not been completed with those fields (setup_status on each record).
The load axis of Figure 2-34. Its title reads Load - Lbs. x 100 while the printed slope (54 lb per inch) and intercept (140 lb) of the fit drawn on it, and the same test LPT 87 on Figure 2-48 (plain Lbs.), only make sense in plain pounds. The data record the axis numbers as pounds and note the title; a reader who knows what the x 100 meant is welcome. The fit line’s intercept read on the axis numbers is 139 lb, beside the printed 140 lb (qa/curves-s2-b1/review.md).
The authors’ straight lines. The fit lines (Slope = ...) and the bearing-capacity line on Figures 2-32 to 2-34 are read like any curve but have no experiment record yet, so they sit in the batch files, not in data/, until the index gains derived-series records for them.
The first inch of Figure 2-48 (Volume I, printed 2-83). Its 0 to 1 in interval is drawn about 233 px tall against 304 to 316 px for every other inch. Both readings take the grid as drawn (the bottom frame is 0 in). If the zero line was meant to sit at the regular spacing, every value below 1 in shifts by up to about 0.25 in. The same test, LPT 87, is printed on Figure 2-34 with a regular first inch, which a comparison of the two printings could use (qa/curves-s2-b2/review.md).
Grid lines beyond the last printed label. On Figures 2-32, 2-34 and 2-45 the frame runs past the last labelled line, and the unlabelled lines there (penetration 10 and 11 in, 7 to 9 in; load 275 and 300 lb) are valued by the even grid spacing. The two readings differ there by at most 0.08 in, because one anchored those lines and the other extrapolated; the record values rest on the anchored lines.

title: Open questions
text:
The audit

Points checked by one reviewer only. Every sampled point is meant to be checked by two students. Where one of the pair has not returned a chunk, the point stands as checked by one person, and its row in qa/audits.csv says so. Nothing in the pipeline waits for the second return; a later wave can re-deal such points if a user needs two signatures on a figure.
Scan of the sample, not the population. The audits cover every disputed point and a sample of the agreed ones, sized by the square root of the points in a figure. An agreed point outside the sample rests on the agreement of two readings made separately and on the rules, not on a person.

title: Open questions
text:
Scope

Not yet read. Most Volume I curves. In Section II, the eight load-penetration figures 2-29, 2-32 to 2-34 and 2-45 to 2-48 and the three DPT signatures of Fig. 2-54 (the dynamic penetrometer) are read; the other load-penetration figures, the pressure parameter plots, the DPT correlation, rate series and density control are not, nor Tables 1-1, 2-1 and 2-2. Of Sections III to V, three impact tests, two model drop tests and the run tables of Fig. 4-6a (drag) and Table 5-3 (model drop) are read; the other impact and drag records are indexed only.
Not yet extracted sources. The Apollo 15 and 16 penetrometer tables and the WES M-71-10 reports are acquired and registered but not yet turned into records; 13 further leads are acquired-with-caveat and await a rights decision each.
Later simulants. Whether data on GRC-1, JSC-1A and their successors enter the first release is undecided (D-015).

title: Open questions
text:
Points counted twice

A curve’s end recorded by both readings. Where the other reading’s last (or first) sample lies just beyond the canonical end of a trace, within both readings’ bounds of that end, the comparison keeps it as a point of its own, so the end is recorded twice, a fraction of a pixel apart. Applied to the batches read before 2026-11-19, the rule that drops such a duplicate would remove 193 points (159 verified on the page by the other agent, 34 one-sided) from the records; the values are not wrong, only counted twice. The rule is used from the dynamic penetrometer batch on (tools/diff_curves.py --end-dedup); whether to apply it to the earlier records, some of whose points the students have audited, is open.

title: Open questions
section: Two printed values for one quantity
text:
Two printed values for one quantity

The touchdown velocities of NASA Tests No. 1 and 2. Table 5-T3 (Volume I, printed 5-45, PDF 325) is in the records b68-mdrop-t5-3-rs and b68-mdrop-t5-3-ss since 2026-11-20, every bed’s relative density, unit weight and friction angle with it, and the record pages of the two tests give its values. Its velocities “were calculated based on the exact time interval between the instant of model release to the instant of ground contact” (printed 5-44, PDF 324). The insets of the strut-load figures print others: -114.93 in./sec. for Test No. 1 (Fig. 5-25, printed 5-50, PDF 330; the table gives -114.9) and, on a degraded scan, -60.55 and 83.75 in./sec. for Test No. 2 (Fig. 5-32, printed 5-57, PDF 337; the table gives -60.5 and 83.5, and 83.75 does not round to 83.5). Our arithmetic, against |V_v| = g tau (the speed of a free fall from rest over tau) within the rounding of both printed numbers: with the report’s g for Earth, 32.2 ft/s^2 (glossary, printed 2-2, PDF 27), three of the four vertical drops are consistent with it and none of the four with a horizontal velocity; with standard gravity, all four vertical drops and one angled drop (Test No. 3). The two values of g differ by 0.08 percent, about the rounding of a printed tau, so at this precision the verdicts depend on the g used. That shows consistency, not the method, which the report does not state (qa/tables-s5-b1/arithmetic.md). Both values are in the records with their sources; which one a simulation starts from is a study’s choice. How the inset values were obtained, and the method behind the angled drops’ velocities, are open.

title: Open questions
text:
How to help

Pick an item, say which, and send what you found with the page, figure and pixel or printed value, so it can enter the record with a citation like every other number here.
If you own or can scan a printed copy of AM-68-1 (Bendix, 1968, both volumes) at 300 dpi or better, items 6 and 7 close almost by themselves.
If you ran, or know who ran, these tests or their plotter, items 3 and 9 are yours.

Every item above names its evidence file in the repository; the decision log (docs/decisions.csv) records what was decided about it and when.

Generated view. Inputs: docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md. Regenerate with python tools/build_site.py; do not edit this file, fix the inputs.

title: Data organization and conventions
text: This is the data dictionary for the repository. It is updated in the same commit as any change to the layout, file formats or vocabularies, so it never lags the data. Version 1, 2026-10-07.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Purpose, in one paragraph
Physical soil-test data from Apollo-era NASA contractor reports is recovered from scanned pages into machine-readable files (SI units), with the test setup, the provenance of every number and the uncertainty of reading it from the page recorded (the experimental uncertainty is known only where repeat tests show it), so that anyone with a simulator can set up these experiments as virtual experiments, as far as the recorded setup allows, and judge the simulator against them (Project Chrono’s soil models are our own first use, in separate repositories since 2026-11-18, D-046). The same organized corpus lets an agent answer questions from the source material with page citations.

Calibration and validation are the user’s choice, not a property of the data (D-028)
Almost any test can serve to calibrate a model or to validate it; which one is a choice made in a particular study, for a particular claim, with a particular model, and others may choose otherwise. The data therefore carries no such roles. It records, for every experiment, the facts any split needs:

What kind of test it is: an element test, in which the soil is in a nearly uniform, known state (direct shear, density limits, grain size), or a boundary-value test, whose response mixes many properties (static load-penetration, dynamic penetrometer); a derived series (an envelope, a friction-angle chart) is a reduction of other tests, not an experiment of its own.
What was measured and how well: the setup and how complete it is (setup_status), the response, and its uncertainty (reading bounds; the scatter of repeat tests where they exist).
How tests depend on each other: same soil, same bed state, same laboratory, and the hard dependencies (relation: same-as, derived-from) that any split must respect so that no data is used on both sides of it.

Notes on what a given test can and cannot pin down for a given kind of model (for example, a direct shear peak constrains a continuum model’s friction coefficient, through a model-specific conversion, but not its stiffness, while a push test mixes friction, density, stiffness and dilation) are documented beside the data, so whoever chooses a split knows what each choice can show. Example splits, with their reasons, belong to studies and to the benchmark’s documentation, never to the data files.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Source identifiers
source_id in sources/register.csv is a short slug: bendix-1968-vol1, bendix-1968-vol2, mdac-1970-cr66914. The corpus folder for a source is named by year and volume where that is unambiguous (corpus/1968/ for Volume I; Volume II will be corpus/1968-vol2/).
Register statuses: lead (identified, not located), located (found, not in hand), acquired (file in nasa-reports/, checksummed), screened (contents inspected and summarized), eligible (holds data in scope), extracted. Dead ends are kept with status not-located and a note of where was searched.
Leads move from sources/leads.csv into the register through a screening batch: tools/promote_leads.py <screened.csv> <leads.csv> <register.csv> --agent <who> --date <when> writes one located row per screened lead (identity fields as the screen confirmed or corrected them against the archive record, the lead’s relation to the Bendix study, and the screening verdict acquire | acquire-with-caveat | lead-only with the setup and text-layer assessment in notes). A row becomes acquired only when the file is downloaded and checksummed: tools/acquire_source.py <source_id> <url>... [--crawl] --date <when> saves the files under nasa-reports/<source_id>/ (a PDS bundle is crawled from its directory listing and kept with its relative paths), writes the SHA-256 digests, page counts and local path into the row and sets the status; a re-run of promote_leads.py keeps those acquisition fields. A single file’s digest goes in the row; a bundle gets nasa-reports/<source_id>/SHA256SUMS.txt (one line per file) and the row holds the digest of that manifest. Videos and high-resolution scans inside a bundle are not tracked by git (.gitignore) but are in the manifest, so the acquisition is reproducible and checkable. The screening submission lives under extractions/<agent>/leads-screen-b<n>/ with its review in qa/leads-screen-b<n>/review.md.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Page identity
Every page has two identities: pdf_page (1-based page in the file we hold) and printed_label (the label printed on the page, for example 2-35). Both are always given together. The map is corpus/<source>/page-map.csv (pdf_page, printed_label, label_source, inferred_label, appendix_heading); inferred_label is the authoritative printed label (OCR misreads are outvoted by the per-section offset). A citation reads: AM-68-1 Vol. I, Fig. 2-21, printed 2-43, PDF 68.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Materials (data/materials/)
materials.csv: one row per soil number as the report defines it (a material in a density state). Columns: soil_no, bendix_designation, description_verbatim, family, state, relative_density, unit_weight_native, unit_weight_unit, unit_weight_N_m3, bulk_density_kg_m3, friction_angle_deg, elastic_modulus_native, elastic_modulus_unit, elastic_modulus_Pa, mean_grain_size_mm, uniformity_coeff, percent_passing_200, d95_mm, read_flags, source_locator, status. Families are the report’s: RS, PS, RSM (a and b are different mixtures and stay separate), RC2, SS, LSM. source_locator names table, printed page, PDF page and row.
specifications.csv: the Appendix A soil specifications (Vol. II, PDF 2 to 98) in long form, one row per soil and quantity, built by tools/build_specifications.py from the canonical page files. Columns: soil_no, quantity, qualifier, value_native, unit_native, value_si, unit_si, printed_text, source_locator, status. Quantities: bendix_designation, relative_density, friction_angle (and friction_angle_band_low/high for LSM), elastic_modulus (qualifier about, as printed or estimated, not measured), modulus_confining_pressure, placement (the printed sentence), roller_count (qualifier passes or rollings, as printed), mix_ratio_by_weight, d50/d10/cu/d95_average and _range (grain size chart inset), gamma_min_label_k and gamma_max_label_k (density chart end labels, pcf and kg/m^3). Each soil’s values come from its own sheet. qa/specifications/table23-vs-appendix-a.md is generated with it and compares every Table 2-3 cell; --check rebuilds both and compares.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Experiments (data/experiments/)
index.csv: one row per physical test, test series or derived series. Columns: experiment_id, source_id, kind, test_type, test_label_printed, soil_family, soil_no, soil_no_status, state_printed, dr_printed, unit_weight_printed_pcf, gp_printed_g, apparatus, penetrator_printed, bin_printed_in, loading, rate_printed, start_depth_printed_in, measured_channels, evidence (figure and table ids, semicolon separated, ortext  (PDF )), setup_status (complete | setup_incomplete | pending), mcc_relevant, priority, relation, relation_target, status, notes. bin_printed_in is the bin or bed as printed, normalized for comparison to A by B in inches, or to A by B [by C] ft when the report gives feet (the model-drop bed and the full-scale pit; until 2026-11-19 the unit was dropped and the site read 18 by 12 ft as inches). relation is same-as | derived-from or empty and relation_target the semicolon-separated ids it points to (from the Volume II batch on; Section II rows leave them empty). The index is built by tools/build_experiments.py from one or more batches of two blind inventories, stacked in order (Section II, experiments-s2-b1; Volume II Appendix C, experiments-vol2c-b1; Volume II Appendices A and B, experiments-vol2ab-b1: grain-size and density charts, friction-angle charts and the sonic moduli; the chemical analyses of Appendix A are material composition, not experiments, and belong in data/materials/; Volume I Sections IV and V, experiments-s3s5-b1: the footpad impact runs with plotted histories and the two model drops with histories, NASA Tests 1 and 2, D-050; Volume I Section IV, experiments-drag-b1: the 13 subscale drag tables, Figs. 4-6a to 4-16, kind run-table, D-050; Volume I Section V, experiments-t5-3-b1: Table 5-T3, the detail correlation drops of the LM model, kind run-table, read in the same blind pass as the table’s cells, 2026-11-20); a later batch’s row with an id already in the index (a test or series printed again) merges into the earlier row: its evidence is added, the earlier cells stand, and the printed facts that differ are noted on the row and listed in index.json (merged_rows). Volume II rows keep the b68 alias with source_id bendix-1968-vol2; envelopes are named by their printed Dr range in hundredths (b68-ds-fc-1a-dr50-57) and stresses in psi with p for the point (b68-ds-fc-7b-n27p1psi). The *_printed columns hold the value exactly as printed beside the test (caption, legend, inset, or the paragraph describing the figure) and are never inferred from another test; they are index fields for finding and matching experiments, and setup.json is where the reconciled SI setup lives. kind is single (one physical test), averaged-series (a curve the report says is averaged from several tests), derived-series (a reduction the authors drew from identified tests, such as a failure envelope), correlation (a fit drawn without the underlying points), summary (a number that exists only in the text), sample (a bin sample analyzed for grain size and min/max density), run-table (a printed table of separate runs of one test type, one physical test per row: the subscale drag tables of Figs. 4-6a to 4-16, one row per printed table page, from 2026-11-19, D-050; Table 5-T3, the eight detail correlation drops, one row per soil family of its beds, b68-mdrop-t5-3-rs and b68-mdrop-t5-3-ss, from 2026-11-20, because the index and the site group records by soil family and the table mixes RS and SS beds; its runs are in runs.csv, below). A run-table whose runs include a drop that has its own record (NASA Tests No. 1 and 2, b68-mdrop-10, b68-mdrop-11) carries relation same-as with those ids, so a split keeps them together. The descriptive columns (apparatus, loading, measured_channels from the first reading, state_printed and test_label_printed from the second) take a value from qa/<batch>/resolutions.csv when one is recorded there, checked on the page (from 2026-11-20, batch experiments-t5-3-b1). soil_no_status is reported | inferred | conflict | unknown; conflict marks a test two figures label with different states (LPT 26 and LPT 27 in Volume I).
experiment_id scheme: <source alias>-<test_type>-<label>, lower case, hyphens only. The alias b68 stands for bendix-1968-vol1. The label is the report’s own test number when one is printed (b68-lpt-027, b68-lpt-064A, b68-dpt-r53958, b68-smp-ssd-4-18), the normal stress for a direct shear test (b68-ds-f2-21-n3520), or, for series without a printed number, the figure id plus a sequence number in legend order or the legend label (b68-lpt-f2-36-s01, b68-dpt-f2-55-rs). Test types: gs grain size, dens min/max, compaction and in-place density, ds direct shear, tx triaxial, lpt static load-penetration, spt static penetrometer, dpt dynamic penetrometer, imp footpad impact, drag footpad drag, mdrop 1/6-scale LM model drop (Section V; id b68-mdrop-<Bendix drop number>, D-050; Table 5-T3’s drops, a run-table, are b68-mdrop-t5-3-<soil family>), sonic sonic modulus, smp bin sample (gs;dens). Impact runs are b68-imp-<run> (subscale, b68-imp-ii-1 for run II-1) and b68-imp-fs<n> (full scale).
Per experiment folder:

setup.json: material and state; preparation (placement method, compaction, waiting time, bed reuse); geometry (bin dimensions and fill depth, penetrator profile and dimensions, specimen dimensions); boundaries (wall and tool materials, applied loads); loading (control, rate history, impact velocity, moving mass, drop height, gravity level); measurement (sensor type and location, filtering, sampling, zero definition); data meaning per series (measurement markers, recorded trace, author fit, computed, derived). Every field is an object {value, unit, status, source} with status in reported | derived | inferred | unknown and source a page locator.
observations.csv: the points, written by tools/build_observations.py from the canonical reading that tools/diff_curves.py selects (see docs/CURVE-READING.md). Columns experiment_id, series_id, panel, point_kind, sequence, x_si, y_si, x_bound_si, y_bound_si, x_native, y_native, x_read_bound, y_read_bound, x_unit_native, y_unit_native, pixel_u, pixel_v, status, source, note. point_kind in marker | trace | gridline | feature; sequence is the point’s number in the reading named by source (its drawing order along the trace in that reading, never sorted by x); pixel_u, pixel_v locate the point on the unrotated 300 dpi page image; the bounds are reading bounds, not standard deviations: from 2026-10-14 (D-025) the largest change of value over the point’s pixel interval on the piecewise map plus the location error of the two lines around it (before: pixel bound times the local scale plus the calibration residual); status in agreed (the two readings matched within the sum of their bounds; for trace samples the other reading is interpolated at the canonical sample’s displacement) | resolved (a page re-read settled a disagreement; the decision row says which reading was right) | one-sided-verified (only one reading holds the point and the other agent verified it on the page image) | one-sided (held by one reading, not verified by anyone) | pending-review | confirmed | audited (from 2026-10-30, roadmap 4c: two student reviewers answered ok on the point in qa/audits.csv, the pair outcome confirmed of tools/ingest_review.py; audited when the two readings had agreed on the point, confirmed when it rested on a rule, a re-read or one reading; the status the readings gave it is kept in the note after audit:; any other pair outcome is noted and changes nothing; a verdict on a reading a decision has since replaced at that sample is noted as superseded and not applied; tools/build_observations.py --audits); source names the reading whose value is kept (<reader>-interp: a value interpolated on that reader’s trace at the displacement of the canonical sample numbered sequence, where a decision kept the other trace). Points of both readings can be in one series (a marker or a curve end only the non-canonical reader recorded), so rows keep the order of the canonical file within a panel and series, which is drawing order. The per-point decisions of a batch live in qa/<batch>/decisions-<figure>-p<n>.csv (the pilot’s were renamed to this pattern on 2026-10-14; columns panel, series_id, point_kind, sequence, source, status, use, note; no source means the canonical reading); use names the reading whose value replaces the canonical one (span instead keeps the value and widens its read bounds to take in the other reading’s value and bound, for a point neither reading could be shown right on, or a peak whose time is a locator on a flat top; 2026-10-27, D-030; the widened bound is rounded up, from 2026-11-19), and a row with status excluded drops the point (for example an interpolation across a visible gap in the drawn line, which is an estimate and not a reading). The decision note is appended to the point’s note after | decision:. Decisions from a blind adjudication are written by its apply script from the round’s answers and key; for a run answered some, the off-line samples come from the round’s off-lists.csv (columns item, adjudicator, sample_px, verdict off|on|unclear: the comment transcribed sample by sample by two independent readers, diffed), never from the comment text; an unclear sample stays undecided (D-039).
series.json: the figure and panel the points came from, each panel’s quantities with native and SI units and the conversion factor used, both readings’ calibration residuals and anchor counts and, for piecewise maps, map (the lines used with their location errors, the lines not on the ink, the number of recovered lines), point counts by status and kind, the batch, the reading-rules version and the canonical-selection rule. Written per batch by tools/build_batch_records.py <batch>.
runs.csv and runs.json (records of kind run-table, written by tools/build_run_table.py <batch> from the cells two transcriptions agreed on, qa/<batch>/agreed.csv of tools/diff_tables.py): one row per printed run, experiment_id, run_number, every printed column in SI (D_m, d_m, VH_m_s, gp_bar_m_s2, Dr, unit_weight_N_m3, FD_N, FV_N, alpha_deg, the derived FD_over_d_gamma_Aft and VH_over_sqrt_dg as printed, FD_over_Aft_Pa, FV_over_Apt_Pa, bulk_density_kg_m3) and as printed (D_in, d_in, VH_fps, gp_bar, gamma_pcf, FD_lb, FV_lb, FD_over_Aft, FV_over_Apt, named by their printed unit, an exception to the *_native names of observations.csv; a column kept as printed is not repeated), status (agreed; pending-review where a cell has no agreed value or an unreadable digit, kept as ? in the printed column with its SI cell empty), check: the row’s results outside the printed rounding and the heuristic area flags of the arithmetic check of the derived columns (tools/check_drag_table.py, qa/<batch>/arithmetic.md), and audit (from 2026-11-21): the run’s cells the student reviewers checked, in printed order, as <printed column> <pair outcome> by <reviewer> (<chunk>), empty until a cell of the run is audited; the run’s status stays as the transcriptions left it, since a sample checks a few of its cells. runs.json audit counts the record’s cells, the cells sampled and the cells two reviewers confirmed. A transcribed number carries the precision of its printing (half a unit of its last digit), not a reading bound; the diameters D and depths d are nominal set points, taken as exact. d is measured from the soil surface to the bottom of the pad at zero pitch (Fig. 4-4), held by locking the loading piston; whether the pad’s pivot was free or clamped is not stated per run. The units of the two pressure columns are not printed (psi is inferred). runs.json names the figure, the method, the columns with their units and factors, the definitions of the derived columns as printed, and the arithmetic check’s summary (the common factor between the two pressure columns, the runs flagged). These are the columns of the drag tables (--family drag, the default). Table 5-T3 (--family mdrop --soil-family <RS|SS>, from 2026-11-20) has its own: experiment_id, run_number (the printed NASA Test No.), bendix_drop_no, same_test_as (the record of the same drop’s time histories, a single mdrop row labeled with that NASA Test No., or empty), in SI VV_m_s, Vh_m_s (touchdown velocities, sign as printed), tau_s (time from model release to touchdown), Dr, unit_weight_N_m3, phi_deg, bulk_density_kg_m3, then soil_printed and the printed VV_in_s, Vh_in_s, gamma_pcf, status, check and audit. A column kept as printed (tau_s, Dr, phi_deg) keeps the printed digits, a leading decimal point included (.298), and a ? the readers could not read. A row without an agreed Soil stops the build rather than fall out of both family records.
A record from several figures (from 2026-11-19, D-050: the vertical impact runs, whose force and displacement against time are Fig. 4-19 and whose force against displacement is Fig. 4-20) numbers its panels across the figures: panel in observations.csv is the record’s panel, given per figure panel by the record_panel column of qa/<batch>/panel-map.csv. Its series.json adds figures (the list; figure_id is the first), and each panel entry gives its figure_id and figure_panel (the panel number on the printed figure, which audit objects and qa/<batch>/ files use); the calibrations are keyed by figure and panel (F4-20/cal-p1). A record’s figures are read in one batch. A one-figure record whose panel is renumbered names its figure and figure panel the same way (each dynamic penetrometer record of Fig. 2-54 is its own panel 1, from the figure’s panel 1, 2 or 3). A panel entry may carry relation (a panel that re-plots another: Fig. 4-20 is derived from Fig. 4-19) and note (what a user of the panel’s values must know, such as a misprinted axis label), both from the panel map. A note may hold several sentences, one per line (from batch curves-s5-b1); the record page joins the notes of all panels and gives a sentence that several panels share once.
series.json breaks (from 2026-11-19, only on records that have one): a drawn line’s explicit breaks, where the scan has no ink and both readers stopped (the dropout on Fig. 4-20), each with the record panel, series_id, the line samples after and before it (source, sequence) and the reason. Written from the hand-made qa/<batch>/breaks.csv (figure_id, figure panel, series_id, after and before as source|sequence, reason; both must be consecutive trace samples of the series in drawing order; optional gap_u1, gap_v1, gap_u2, gap_v2, from batch curves-s5-b1: the two ends of the gap, measured on the page in pixels). The plots do not draw the line across a break, and the record page names it (the reason up to its first semicolon; what follows, such as who found the break, stays on the review page). The comparison does not interpolate the other (non-canonical) reading across a break either (from 2026-11-19: tools/reconcile_curves.py maps the gap’s ends on each reading’s own calibration and passes the spans to tools/diff_curves.py --break-a, --break-b, or, for a break without pixels, the span between the two samples named, --break): a sample beside a break is compared directly with the other reading’s nearest sample on an intact stretch, within both bounds, as at the end of a trace, never through the break. Rows of observations.csv are in drawing order within a series; sequence is each reading’s own numbering, not an order. Two rows in drawing order may share an x value (two samples read at one time on a steep flank), so x is not strictly increasing.

Re-derivation and calibration files of a curve batch (D-025), written by tools/reconcile_curves.py <batch> from the submissions, never edited: qa/<batch>/rederived/<reader>/<figure>/points-p<n>-native.csv (the reader’s pixels on its piecewise map, with cal_model) and cal-p<n>/ (calibration.json as submitted, anchors.csv with any recovered line, knots.json: per axis the lines used, their tilt, location error and distances from the ink, and the lines rejected with the reason); qa/<batch>/calibration-sensitivity.md (affine against piecewise values per canonical series); qa/<batch>/canonical-<figure>-p<n>.csv and qa/<batch>/canonical.csv (the canonical points: each point’s own columns, then status, source, other_x_native, other_y_native, decision_note, other_pixel_u, other_pixel_v; the last two, added 2026-11-18, give the other reading’s place on the page, which audit packets draw). Inputs written by hand: qa/<batch>/ink-checks.csv (written by tools/check_trace_ink.py, D-031; columns figure_id, panel, reader, series_id, point_kind, sequence, pixel_u, pixel_v, verdict eligible | excluded | review, line_ink_px, symbol, reason, image_sha, params) is read by tools/reconcile_curves.py by default since 2026-10-30 (D-032): an excluded sample of either reading leaves the comparison as a hand exclusion would, its note starts with D-031 ink check, and the diff report lists every hand decision it overrides; review samples stay. Inputs written by hand: qa/<batch>/overlays.csv (optional cal_a, cal_b: a reading’s calibration directory when it is not cal-p<n> next to its points file) and qa/<batch>/knots.csv (figure_id, panel, reader, x_value, y_value, u, v, x_source, y_source, note: a line a reader left out, measured on the page), and qa/<batch>/feature-roles.csv (figure_id, panel, reader, series_id, sequence, submitted_role, role, reason; from batch curves-s5-b1, 2026-11-19): a feature whose note names its role by another convention than the batch’s (there: a compression panel’s peaks and minima named by the curve as drawn instead of the signed value). tools/reconcile_curves.py checks every row against the submissions before writing anything (known figure, panel and reader; role and submitted_role two different words of knee, minimum, knee, peak, first, last; one row per feature; the submitted note opening with exactly submitted_role) and stops on any failure; it then writes the rederived note as <role> (role renamed by qa/<batch>/feature-roles.csv; submitted note: <the note verbatim>), so that the two readings pair by role. The submission is not touched. qa/<batch>/panel-map.csv may carry a figure_id column when a batch’s figures differ in units. A calibration of a log or reciprocal axis (D-027) records x_transform or y_transform (log10, reciprocal; absent means linear) in calibration.json and knots.json; its anchors keep the printed values, while ax, ay, the residuals and x_per_px, y_per_px are in the plotting coordinate q = T(value). Points are always written in the printed unit; a read bound on such an axis is the larger half of the interval mapped back from q (the tools count the values whose two halves differ by more than 10 percent), and the SI conversion applies to the value, never to q.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Figures index (corpus/<source>/figures.csv)
One row per figure or table, built by tools/build_figures.py from two blind inventories and a resolutions file (qa/<batch>/resolutions.csv: id, column, value, status, note). Columns: id, kind, title_as_printed, printed_page, pdf_page, test_type, soils, states, apparatus, rate_or_dynamics, data_form, panels, curves, trace_classes, x_quantity, x_unit, x_unit_as_printed, x_axis_type, y_quantity, y_unit, y_unit_as_printed, y_axis_type, legend_entries, rotation, in_scope, transcribe, priority, mcc_relevant, status, notes_claude, notes_codex.
Ids are F<section>-<n> and T<section>-<n> in Volume I. In Volume II (corpus/1968-vol2/) numbered figures keep the printed number with the appendix letter, FA-12, FC-1B, and FB-3 for the figures numbered 1 to 8 inside the reproduced IITRI report of Appendix B; unnumbered tables are identified by page locator TA-pNNN, NNN the PDF page where the table starts (the chemical analyses and normative mineral tables of the soil specifications). When the two submissions used different id schemes, qa/<batch>/id-aliases.json maps the first submission’s ids to the canonical ones before the diff; the sidecar records the map.
Volume II adds three columns after pdf_page and before status: appendix (A, B, C) and relation, relation_target with vocabulary same-as | derived-from | reproduces | unresolved | none (a reproduction is the same content printed again, as the four figures repeated under each soil of a material; derived-from points at the figure or table the data came from, across volumes: F2-14, F2-17, F2-23 and Table 2-3 of Volume I derive from Appendix A and B figures; unresolved is a plausible but unconfirmed link). One agent’s none yields to the other’s stated relation (absence is not a reading), status vocabulary-resolved.
Volume I Sections III to V (batch inventory-s3s5-b1, 2026-11-19, D-050: Section III, Section IV to Fig. 4-22, Section V to Fig. 5-39) are appended to corpus/1968/figures.csv after the Section II rows. They add section (III, IV, V) after pdf_page, and relation, relation_target as in Volume II; the Section II rows leave all three empty. A printed item continued over several scanned pages has one row per page, the first keeping the printed id and the others -pNNN (T5-2-p309, the continuation of Table 5-T2; F5-2-p285, the second frame of a foldout); an alias of the form <id>@<pdf_page> in qa/<batch>/id-aliases.json maps a submission that repeated an id on several pages. TABLE 5-T2 is T5-2.
The rest of Section V and Section VI (batch inventory-s6-b1, 2026-11-20, D-050: Figs. 5-40 to 5-47 and 6-1 to 6-27, PDF 345 to 440) are appended after them, section V or VI. Section VI prints its four tables as numbered figures (Figs. 6-4, 6-6, 6-8, 6-10: kind figure, data_form table). Each of the eight detail correlation drops (NASA Drop No. 1 to 8) has a four-sheet figure of measured histories with the report’s computed curves (Figs. 6-11 and 6-13 to 6-19) and a four-sheet figure of computed curves alone at a higher strut damping (Figs. 6-12 and 6-20 to 6-26), one row per sheet. A history sheet is same-as Fig. 6-10, the table of the eight drops (its drop’s NASA and Bendix numbers are in the row’s notes), and, for NASA Drops 1 and 2, the Section V figures of the same channels: same-as here means the same test and channel, not the same trace, since the two printings have not been compared and can differ. The computed-only sheets are derived-from Fig. 6-10 and in_scope no; Figs. 6-4, 6-6 and 6-8 reprint rows of Table 5-T2 and are reproduces, in_scope no. qa/inventory-s6-b1/corrections.csv changes cells both readers agreed on, each with its page evidence, as Volume II’s does. The brief of this batch asked for the controlled unit codes, so *_unit_as_printed is empty on its rows (--unit-codes; the printed form is in the notes); in any batch a code with an underscore (in_s) is never taken for a printed spelling. A row a correction changed has the status resolved.
Vocabularies: axis_type in linear | log | normalized | reciprocal | n/a (normalized: a dimensionless quantity on a linear scale; reciprocal: the 1/gamma scale of the unit weight charts); unit in inch | lb | psf | psi | pcf | g | s | mm | percent | deg | ksi | none | n/a, with ms | ft_s | in_s | in_s2 | deg_s | ustrain since Sections III to V (milliseconds, feet and inches per second, inches per second squared, degrees per second, microinches per inch) and deg_s2 since Section VI (degrees per second squared, the vehicle pitch acceleration), with the printed spelling kept in *_as_printed (an axis multiplier such as “x 10^-3”, “(x 10^1)” or a leading “1,000” belongs to the quantity and is stripped before the unit is normalized); test_type in grain size | density | bed preparation | direct shear | triaxial | load penetration | dynamic penetrometer | drag | impact | model drop | sonic | soil model | soil properties | apparatus | other (model drop: the 1/6-scale LM model landings of Section V); data_form in table | curve | schematic | photo | text | mixed; trace_classes from measurement-markers | recorded-trace | author-fit | computed | schematic | setup-evidence.
Three columns carry judgment and follow fixed rules (decided 2026-10-07):

in_scope (yes | maybe | no): the item carries numbers to extract into data/. transcribe is yes for every page of a section in the transcription scope, so photographs and conceptual charts reach the corpus without being “in scope” for extraction.
priority: 1 = needed for the first calibration and prediction protocols (shear family, LPT records with known bed state, DPT signatures and correlation, materials tables); 2 = needed to set up or interpret those tests (bed preparation, boundary and bin effects, rate series, degradation); 3 = context only.
mcc_relevant (yes | maybe | no): yes only when the figure shows the same material after different loading or handling histories with a different response, plus the state maps needed to read those figures; the column answers one question, whether any test demands a history-dependent model.

Conventions fixed in the Volume II batch (2026-10-07) and applied from then on: a photograph has 0 panels and 0 curves and priority 3; a plot with an inset table of numbers or printed fit parameters is mixed, a data sheet whose legend lists the test identities is curve; a figure or table that reproduces another is in_scope no and priority 3 (the first printing holds the numbers; the page is still transcribed); a chemical analysis is priority 2 (material identity, not a simulation input); a normative mineral analysis of a reference rock is not soil data (in_scope no, priority 3); a per-soil summary curve derived from primary figures is priority 2 when the primaries are 1; a computed curve is in_scope no.
Curve-count convention: every drawn line is a trace, including each boundary of a shaded or bracketed range; markers and the fitted line through them are one response series (range bars on a marker are part of the marker); construction guides are not counted. Row status: agreed (every reconciled cell agreed), resolved (some cells settled by a vocabulary rule, a page re-read, a convention or a scope rule, each recorded in the sidecar), provisional (a count or grade to be re-done at extraction or decided by Dan), pending-review, and one-sided-verified for a row that only one submission listed and that entered through qa/<batch>/row-decisions.csv (id, decision, status, note saying how the row was verified against the page image). The sidecar figures.json lists the rules, per-cell statuses with their notes, and the other agent’s text for every descriptive cell that differs.
Known source quirks recorded here because the index is where an agent will meet them: “SS” in a soil designation is silica sand, but “SS Drag Tests” (Figure 2-60) and the test numbers “SSD” mean subscale drag; LPT 27 is captioned RS Dense in Figure 2-29 and RS Intermediate in Figure 2-43; the ordinate of Figure 2-34 is printed “Lbs. x 100” although the ticks and the printed slope are in pounds; Table 1-1 prints soil 4 at 50.5 pcf where Table 2-3 prints 50.6.
Volume II quirks: the Appendix C computer plots are bound out of order (PDF 147 = C-35, 148 = C-34, 149 = C-33) and Appendix B keeps the IITRI report’s own page numbers, both handled by corpus/1968-vol2/page-map-corrections.csv; Figure A-45, captioned “Photomicrograph RSM Soil” under soil 12 (RSM-b), is the same photograph as A-17 (RSM-a); the Volcalite chemical analysis is printed seven times with two different typesetting slips (A-72 drops the MgO line and prints 5.58 against CaO; A-81 prints MgO 1.61 and drops Na2O) and the clay analysis twice with iron oxide 1.1 (A-72) against 1.2 (A-81); the computer-fitted envelopes print “Angle of Friction”, “Tan Theta” and “Cohesion” with axes in tens of psf; Figure C-7A to C-7C (RSM-b) are in psi from a different apparatus; the SS series at Dr .30, .48 and .77 in C-5A and C-20 are credited to Bendix report MM-65-2 (as printed on C-15), not to this study; the sonic moduli of soils 5, 10 and 12 in Table 2-3 are estimates, not measurements (A-41, A-79, A-93); the text gives phi for soil 11 as about 38.3 and for soil 12 as about 37 degrees (A-84, A-93) where Table 2-3 prints 42 and 48; soil 12 was rolled “10 passes per two inch layer” (A-93) where Volume I printed 2-113 says twenty-four rolls.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Reading bounds and agreement
A reading bound is a half-width in native units built from: half the visible marker or trace width; the axis-calibration residual; placement repeatability; extra ambiguity from overlap, damage or uncertain centering. Bounds are bounds, not standard deviations. Two agents agree on a matched point when |xA - xB| <= bxA + bxB and |yA - yB| <= byA + byB (in log coordinates on log axes; on steep curves the x bound is propagated into y). Printed numbers (tables) must agree exactly after typography normalization. Agreed objects take status=agreed; disagreements go to review and come back confirmed or interval; a stratified 5 to 10 percent of agreed objects is audited and marked audited. Readings are never averaged; the canonical trace is the one named by the rule recorded in series.json.

Reviewer audits (qa/audits.csv and qa/audits/)
qa/audits.csv holds one row per reviewer and point actually checked by a person: batch, object (<figure_id>/<panel>/<series_id>/<point_kind>/<source>/<sequence>: sequence numbers the points of the reading named in source, so an audit stays with its point when a re-reconciliation changes the canonical reading), column (position for a curve sample or compare row, position+identity for a symbol, position for a symbol whose identity answer is listed in qa/audits/voided.csv for that chunk, position+value for a cell of a transcribed table, whose object is <table>/1/<column>/cell/agreed/<row key>, since 2026-11-21, D-050), auditor (initials), date, outcome (ok | problem | cannot tell | unreadable), note (starts with the chunk and the reviewer’s letter, chunk W1-07 (R1-D), then the reviewer’s comment). The file is append-only and never holds the same object and auditor twice; a point’s pair outcome (confirmed, flagged, split for ok against problem, cannot-tell, a mix such as ok + cannot tell where the definite answers agree, single) is computed from all its rows when a report is made, never stored (tools/ingest_review.py, pair_outcome).
The audit in brief. Each wave samples points of figures already read: every compare row (up to a cap), every resolved or unverified one-sided point, some verified one-sided points, and agreed points in a number that grows with the square root of the figure’s point count. The sample is cut into chunks of about 60 rows, and each chunk is checked against the scan by two reviewers, or by one in a second-review chunk that completes an earlier chunk; the first audit of the grain-size curves and of the newest test families has one reviewer per chunk, their second reviews following in a later release (D-050). Every chunk also carries seeded attention checks whose answers are known; a return that misses one is not recorded unless the maintainers accept it, and one they decline is never recorded, its points going to another reviewer. An answer a reviewer could not give fairly (for example on a figure the packet showed upside down) is voided in qa/audits/voided.csv and asked again. A point two reviewers answered ok becomes audited or confirmed; every other outcome is noted on the point. The blind adjudication on the scan (D-023) takes every point with two or more reviews that is not confirmed, and every point a single reviewer marked as a problem; a point with one review that is not a problem waits for its second review. The program’s manual (docs/audit/README.md), its packet tool and its answer keys stay out of the public release while the audit runs. In the maintainers’ repository the files under qa/audits/ and their columns are listed in that manual, among them the reviewer’s left date in reviewers.csv, the repeats column of assignments.csv (a second-review chunk, one reviewer, D-037) and the controls vocabulary of returns-log.csv (passed | accepted | missed | declined). qa/<batch>/audit-meta.json carries, per figure, the series labels and symbols, panel names and axis types, rotation, the legend hint and the notes a reviewer sees in about-the-figures.txt; it is drafted by the packet tool from the batch’s maps and the figures index and then edited by hand. A table batch (one with agreed.csv and no canonical.csv) has a hand-written audit-meta.json (kind table: the page image, its rotation, the key column, every printed column with its heading, aliases by which the readers’ notes name a column, and the arithmetic checks and verdicts that flag a column, check_columns and flag_verdicts) and qa/<batch>/cell-layout.csv, written by tools/locate_table_cells.py: one row per box (figure_id, key, column, role cell, key or header, x0 y0 x1 y1 in the upright, straightened frame, u v the center on the scan, bu bv half its size there, deskew_deg), so a packet can show a reviewer the cell, its row key and its column heading.


Typography rule for text cells
When two readings of a text cell differ only by a hyphen or a space at a printed line break (for example “Wedron 4040 narrowly graded” against “Wedron 4040-narrowly graded”), the canonical text keeps the printed hyphen and drops the wrap space, the cell is marked typography-resolved, and it is included in the audit sample so a person confirms the rule did the right thing. Any other text difference is a disagreement for review.


Cell and row status vocabulary
Cell statuses, recorded in the sidecar: agreed (identical after typography normalization), typography-resolved (rule above), uncertain (identical readings, but both agents flagged the glyph; goes to review), pending-review (readings differ; the cell is left empty in data/), confirmed (a person settled it against the scan), interval (the scan does not support one value; bounds given). Row status: agreed when every cell is agreed; resolved-with-notes when some cells are typography-resolved or uncertain; partial when any cell is pending review.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Corpus pages (corpus/<source>/pages/pNNNN.md)
Transcribed under docs/PAGE-TRANSCRIPTION.md: two agents type the page from its 300 dpi image, tools/diff_pages.py compares the two, differences are settled by a page re-read recorded in qa/<batch>/decisions.csv (page, diff_id, use, note), and the canonical page is written from the first submission with the decisions applied. The header carries review_status (agreed, resolved, pending), both transcribers, the batch and the number of differences.
YAML header: source, pdf_page, printed_label, section, figures, tables, rotation, review_status (agreed | confirmed | pending), image. Body: the page text as Markdown with LaTeX math; tables as Markdown tables; per figure a block with caption, axes (label and unit verbatim per axis), legend, description. Curve values are never in page files.

Corpus indexes (corpus/<source>/{contents,equations,symbols,glossary}.csv)
Built from the page files by tools/build_indexes.py (deterministic; --check compares a fresh build with the committed files). Every row carries source, pdf_page, printed_page and the page’s review_status, so a row is as trustworthy as the page it came from.

contents.csv: section, title, level per printed heading (section numbers as printed; an unnumbered appendix title carries its letter). Inside an appendix, a section lettered on the page is prefixed with the appendix letter (B/C is section C, RESULTS, of the IITRI report reproduced as Appendix B, not Appendix C), and each Appendix A soil sheet is A/soil n. A page with no printed number has printed_page empty (the cover and title pages of the IITRI report); unknown is not used, because the absence is known.
equations.csv: number, latex, context per display equation; number is the printed number beside it or empty; context is the end of the sentence that introduces it. Printed duplicates stay (Vol. I Section II numbers two different equations 3-1, printed 2-40 and 2-60).
symbols.csv: symbol, meaning, units, equation per entry of a printed “where” list (X = meaning, or X is the meaning as in Appendix B); equation is the numbered equation the list follows, when there is one.
glossary.csv: term, definition from the report’s own list of abbreviations (Vol. I 2.1.1); a definition printed without its term keeps term empty (the “Dense” entry on printed 2-2).

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Insights (insights/)
One Markdown file per theme (for example soil-selection.md, bed-preparation.md, dpt-as-density-proxy.md). Each paragraph ends with its citation in the form above. These capture judgment and recommendations, not numbers.

title: Data organization and conventions
text:
Site (site/)
A Quarto website generated from the repository by tools/build_site.py (decided 2026-10-07, D-012 to D-014 in docs/decisions.csv). Rules:

Every page is a generated view; no fact is typed into a page. Each page ends with a note naming its inputs and the regeneration command. The generated .qmd files are committed so that a change in what the site says appears in git diff beside the data change that caused it.
The generator is deterministic (sorted keys, fixed formatting, LF, UTF-8) and writes nothing time- or commit-dependent into a page body. python tools/build_site.py --check regenerates into a temporary directory and compares byte for byte with site/; any difference, or any .qmd under site/ the script did not write, fails. Hand edits cannot survive a build.
tools/render_site.py regenerates, writes the render-time footer (site/_footer.html: repository revision, dirty flag, render date) and the recent-changes list (site/_changes.md from git log), both ignored by git, then runs quarto render site (or --preview). site/_site/ and site/.quarto/ are build outputs and are not tracked. Do not leave --preview running while build_site.py rewrites the sources: on 2026-11-19 it rendered changed pages beside their sources (193 stray files under site/); to look at the site, render and serve site/_site/ as static files.
After every change that affects pages, the rendered pages are visited before the work is called done (2026-11-19, Dan): python tools/check_site_layout.py --shots loads every page in headless Edge at 1280 px and 390 px and reports any table that crosses the “On this page” column, reaches past the text column, is wider than the column without a scrolling box, or squeezes a cell to six lines or more; it exits 1 on any of these, and its screenshots of one page of each kind (work/site-check/shots/) are looked at by eye. Every table goes in a box that scrolls sideways (site/table-wrap.lua, a Pandoc filter, so the pages copied from docs/ are covered too; Quarto’s listing tables scroll by site/site.css), and the same filter sets each table’s column widths from its content, the same in every browser (from 2026-11-20, on Dan’s look at the Materials page: left to the browser, a short column could be as wide as a text column and the last column squeezed): a column’s share is its preferred width in characters (its longest cell, capped at 28 so long text wraps, never less than its longest unbreakable piece), and the table is as wide as the text column, or wider, scrolling in its box, when the columns do not fit side by side at their least widths (the longest unbreakable piece; on a phone also 20 characters for a column of longer text, so it scrolls rather than wrapping a text column to a word per line). Pandoc’s equal widths from the dashes of a pipe table stay off (tbl-colwidths: false); the virtual experiment card keeps its own widths. A long code with no spaces gets line-break opportunities after _, ; and , (table() in tools/build_site.py).
Every factual display carries its provenance and a status; missing values are written as not reported, not yet extracted, unreadable, conflicting evidence or not applicable, never as a blank or a zero; counts that measure different things (indexed records, single tests, complete setups, extracted series, recorded audits) are shown separately.
Record pages are written for a user of the data and carry only what that user needs: a descriptive title, a one-paragraph summary, one note on trust and completeness, the data (plot in SI units with the other tests of the figure in gray, downloads, a reading-bounds line, a link to the scan check on the figures page), the reproduce table (value, as printed, where; fields per test type; persistent ambiguities stated and labeled as our observation), the family, the source pages and the citation. From 2026-11-20 (Dan): the line says “reading bounds” (our reading of the figure, not the test’s uncertainty), a dimensionless value is written without a unit (a percent stored as a fraction in percent), and gravity is the report’s value for Earth, 32.2 ft/s^2 (9.81456 m/s^2; glossary, printed 2-2, PDF 27; until 2026-11-20 the pages said, wrongly, that the report does not state it). From 2026-11-21 (Dan): every record plot is drawn as the pilot’s was (tools/figures/plot_observations.py --readable): values with an SI prefix that keeps the tick labels short (mm, kPa, MPa for a modulus, kN/m^3), a long axis title wrapped onto two lines, the title in words, and no caption baked into the image, since the page’s caption says what the markers and error bars mean. Everything written for the maintainers (index-row reconciliation, point status counts, calibration residuals, the agents’ notes, audit status) is on the record’s provenance page review/<record>.qmd, linked from the record page (D-019, 2026-10-08).
docs/decisions.csv (id, date, question, options, decision, who, note) is the decision log; an empty decision means the question is open. Ids are stable (D-001, …). The public release carries a curated log under the same ids, with the columns id, date, question, options and decision (D-052): docs/decisions-public.csv (id, publish, question, options, decision) holds one row per decision, publish either as-is (the other fields empty) or edited, and for an edited one every field given: its public text, or = to keep the original; tools/make_public_release.py builds the log from it and refuses a decision with no row, a doubled id, a row of the wrong width, or an edited row with an empty field. Edited decisions leave out the people and the logistics of the review.
Reader-facing pages (plan v3 Part A, approved 2026-11-05) are written for people at the level of a junior mechanical engineering undergraduate: impersonal and timeless wording, no internal words. Every code (soil, test, symbol) carries its definition: a span of class term with the definition as its title, shown on hover and, through tabindex, on tap or keyboard focus (term() in the generator). The build fails (undefined_terms(), A2.3) when a page of PILOT_PAGES has a definition span whose text is not a code of TERMS or whose title is not that code’s definition, or uses a code whose first use, in reading order over the title, the subtitle and the body (link text and image descriptions included; code spans, link targets, attributes and comments left out), is neither a definition span nor written in parentheses after its plain name (define(): “red scoria (RS)”).

Navigation (plan v3, A5.1): Find a test (experiments/), Soils (materials/), Simulate a test (simulate/), Glossary (glossary/), Download (downloads/), About (about/), plus search. The footer links About, Contribute (contribute/) and Project records (records/). Project records holds the maintainers’ material, public but off the reader’s path: decisions, review, open questions, methods, insights, figures and sources (and the roadmap on the maintainers’ own build; the public release leaves it out, D-052), with the coverage matrix, the five counts, the open decisions and the recent changes that the first build’s overview carried. The landing page (index.qmd) carries the approved wording, a counts line generated from the data and the soils by code and name.
The record pages are being moved to a template built around the virtual experiment card (below). During the pilot only PILOT_RECORD (b68-lpt-024) uses it; the other record pages keep the template of rule 5 until the pilot is approved, then all move.

Virtual experiment card
The card of a test lists what one would need to set up the same test in a simulator (plan v3, A3). It is organized in groups that fit a tool test and will also fit a vehicle on terrain, so a later kind of test fills the same groups rather than starting a new format:

Every entry is a triple (kind, text, where printed). kind is one of three, shown with a visible tag: test (reported: given by the report for this test or its apparatus, or for the procedure of these tests in general, which the text then says), ref (soil reference: a property of the soil from another table of the report, for the soil’s nominal state; Codex, 2026-11-05: a nominal density at one relative density must not read as the measured state of a bed at another), choice (left to the user: an input the report does not give, with what it says around it). An empty group is shown as not given, never dropped. where printed gives the figure, table or section with the printed and the PDF page, as a link to the page image (page_link(); the images come from tools/render_pages.py into the thumbnail cache, and copy_thumbs() reports any that is missing). The card is built by card_lpt() in tools/build_site.py from the index row, the soil table, the figures index, the record’s points, the page transcriptions and the report’s density chart of the soil (DENSITY_CHART); setup.json (Experiments, above) will carry the same groups and kinds, as typed values with units, when it is written.

title: Appendix C computer plots: the drawn lines against the printed fits
text:
Note



Review status: pending. Written from a first read of the pages; quote with that caveat until the page transcriptions are reconciled.


Source: AM-68-1 Vol. II (NASA CR-92215), Appendix C, Figs. C-8 to C-15 (printed C-24 to C-37, PDF 138 to 151). Each of these fourteen plots shows the peak shear stresses of one group of direct shear tests (triangles), a straight line, and a box that prints the group’s average density, angle of friction, tan theta and cohesion: the least-squares fit of the group, computed on a Univac 1107 and plotted on a CAL-COMP plotter (Appendix C text, printed C-1, PDF 115). Both agents read all fourteen blind (batches curves-appc-b7 to -b9, 2026-10-14); each reader also compared its own traced line with the printed box, without moving any point toward it. Findings, 2026-10-15:

The two readings agree on every drawn line: a least-squares line through each reader’s trace samples gives slopes within 0.0017 and intercepts within 6 psf of the other reader’s, on all fourteen plots. What follows is a property of the pages, not of a reading.

A reading bound of a trace sample is about 20 psf, so C-9B, C-9C, C-10B, C-11A, C-13, C-14 and C-15 differ beyond it over much of the line. The grid of these plots is drafted unevenly (about 299 px for the first 1000 psf of shear strength, 287 px for the fifth); both readings use the piecewise map between the drawn lines (D-025), so this is accounted for; and a calibration error would not give offsets of opposite sign and different size on pages that carry the same printed grid.

Where the tests of a computer plot are identified, a least-squares line through the peaks of their data sheets, as read in curves-appc-b1 to -b3, reproduces the printed box: C-9A from the seven tests of Fig. C-1D (zero-stress test included) 1.313 and 630 psf against 1.3059 and 634.20; C-10A from the six tests of Fig. C-2B 0.950 and 489 psf against 0.9471 and 488.69; C-12 from the five tests of Fig. C-4B 0.927 and 137 psf against 0.9349 and 145.81 (the C-12 relation to C-4B was marked unresolved in the index; this supports it). Fig. C-14: the printed cohesion is negative (-109.97 psf); the drawn line instead starts at the frame’s origin corner and ends near the printed line’s end, as if the plotter had clipped the line at the frame and drawn it from there (a hypothesis; nothing else on the page says so).
Fig. C-13: the first character of the printed cohesion is a 1 overstruck with a bar, so the value is -1.87 or 11.87 (as the page transcription already records); the triangles fit 0.567 and 32 psf and the line 0.556 and 50 psf, so neither settles it.

For use of the data: the printed angle, tan theta and cohesion of each box are the authors’ fits, and on at least four plots they are reproducible from the data sheets; the drawn lines are kept in the records as read, with this note, and should not be used as the fits. The triangles are the evidence of the tests. A check against the data sheets of the remaining plots (C-9B, C-10B, C-10C, C-11B, C-11C, C-13 to C-15, whose tests are not all identified) is open.
